subject: Coordinating cross-region demo windows — proposal and options
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0400
Subject: Research Ops demo needs — coordinating times across teams

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're excited to see Redwood's serving demos focused on throughput and cost controls. Our core stakeholders for this call are in multiple time zones: me (EST), Priya (PST), and Dr. Chen (Central). We also have a few engineering folks in APAC (IST/AWST) who would like to join live if possible.

Quick ask: can you propose 2–3 time windows that your EU team can reliably staff (and who would present)? We have two constraints: (1) prefer a slot that lets our PMs join during their workday, (2) keep the session to 45–60 minutes. We're aware of DST issues later in the year — our procurement timeline runs through October so we want something that will remain viable when clocks change.

Initial availability (our side):
- Tue/Wed mornings EST (08:00–11:00 EDT)
- Tue afternoons PST (13:00–16:00 PDT)
- We can do occasional evenings (after 19:00 EDT) if needed

If it helps, happy to split into two 30-min focused sessions (platform & security) to catch more zones.

Thanks,
Sam
Senior Product Manager, Acme Health
Acme Health | sam.torres@acmehealth.com

Hi Sam — thanks, this is really helpful context.

Short answer: yes — we can staff live presenters from our EU team and offer a couple of formats that respect the zones you've listed. A few practical notes up front:
- Europe (CEST) is currently UTC+2 in August; US is on DST (EDT/PDT) so overlaps shift in November.
- To avoid fragile single-slot plans, I recommend either a) one 60-min session at a compromise UTC time, or b) two 30-min slices (core product + security) scheduled so each core audience gets daytime coverage.

Option A — single 60-min (compromise):
- Proposed time: 15:00 CEST / 09:00 EDT / 06:00 PDT — this hits US morning and late EU afternoon. APAC participants would need to join early evening (e.g., IST ~ 18:30).
- Who: Jonas (serving/runtime deep-dive) + me (deployment/offers) + Marissa for procurement/next steps.

Option B — split 2x30-min (preferred for coverage):
- Session 1 (product deep-dive): 14:00 CEST / 08:00 EDT / 05:00 PDT — focused on runtime and performance, led by Jonas (30 min + Q&A).
- Session 2 (security/procure): 19:00 CEST / 13:00 EDT / 10:00 PDT — focused on compliance, demo of controls, led by Marissa.
- Both sessions recorded; each will include a 10-min Q&A.

Notes about DST: after the US clocks roll back in Nov we expect the EDT->CET offset to change by one hour which will make some suggested windows shift by an hour. If you expect final procurement in October, Option B lets you keep meaningful live overlap without rebooking.

I've attached a quick agenda and a timezone matrix that maps the options to your listed participants. If you prefer we can also propose a rotating weekly slot for follow-ups.

Which option looks better for your stakeholders? If you confirm, I'll send calendar invites and a short agenda.

Best,
Naomi
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Sam — quick technical note on the sessions. If you choose the split approach, I can keep the product deep-dive to ~25 minutes: 10m architecture, 10m live perf demo with a shorter prompt set (we'll use a cached KV prefix so we can show tail latency reliably), 5m Q&A. That keeps the slot tight for APAC colleagues who might join just for the demo segment.

Also: for the security/procure session Marissa has a pre-built slide deck with SOC2 and data flow diagrams that shortens review time. Happy to include a 1-page follow-up that lists recommended config profiles (batching/caching/quant) best for cost predictability.

Jonas

- Our Chief Data Scientist (Dr. Chen) may only join the first 30 mins; can you make sure the product deep-dive covers model stability under load early in the session?

Appreciate the flexibility — splitting is a good compromise given our APAC folks.
